body:
I'm a Windows user and thought it would be nice to have Windows developer documentation, like the Ubuntu one. I spun up a VM so I could make sure I documented all the necessary steps.

- Install [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org) and accept defaults
  - When the install finishes, in the console that opens type:
`pacman -Syu`
  - Reopen the console if it closes (MSYS2 MSYS), and continue to run the command until there are no more updates.
  - Install the ART dependencies:
`pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-x86_64-gdb mingw-w64-x86_64-make mingw-w64-x86_64-pkg-config mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-x86_64-ninja mingw-w64-x86_64-gtkmm3 mingw-w64-x86_64-lcms2 mingw-w64-x86_64-fftw mingw-w64-x86_64-exiv2 mingw-w64-x86_64-lensfun mingw-w64-x86_64-libiptcdata mingw-w64-x86_64-gtk3 mingw-w64-x86_64-mimalloc mingw-w64-x86_64-opencolorio mingw-w64-x86_64-libraw`
- Install [cmake](https://cmake.org/download/#latest)
- Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/Download)
  - Open Visual Studio
  - Open the extensions marketplace (Ctrl+Shift+X) and install `C/C++ Extension Pack`
  - Choose File, Open Folder..., and choose the root ART folder
  - Choose to trust the authors
  - You should get a popup saying "Compiler kits may be present in these directories", with a list of directories from your MSYS2 installation. Choose the Yes option to set up the compiler kits. If the popup goes away you can open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and choose `CMake: Scan for Kits` to open it again.
  - Open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and choose `CMake: Set Launch/Debug Target`. First you'll be prompted to select a kit. Choose `CC xx.x.x x86_64-w64-mingw32 (mingw64)`, where xx.x.x is the version number of the compiler you have installed. Wait until VS is done configuring the project, then you will be prompted to choose a launch target. Choose `art (Install)`.
  - By default the debug configuration will be selected. If you'd like to build a different one, open the command palette and choose `CMake: Select Variant`.
  - In Visual Studio press Shift+F5 to start debugging.
title: Windows build documentation
